Timestamp Deadlines

Frozen 4.0 — epoch milliseconds, duration seconds and elapsed budgets

**Unsigned floating truncation — 24 October 2026:** [Correction and limits](../UNSIGNED-FLOATING-TRUNCATION.md) truncate finite float/double operands before unsigned range checks, allowing(-1,0) to become unsigned zero. Adds60 constructor/cast/reference/castable cases; exact overflow thresholds and nonfinite errors remain intact. Source1.25.1 unpublished/public1.25.0 accepted; REQ-126 partial. **Unsigned Decimal truncation — 24 October 2026:** [Correction and limits](../UNSIGNED-DECIMAL-TRUNCATION.md) discard numeric fractions before unsignedLong range facets/backing selection, with48 constructor/cast/reference/castable cases. Fractional lexical forms still refuse; floating near-zero consistency remains separate. Source1.25.1 unpublished/public1.25.0 accepted; REQ-126 partial. **Exact floating integer boundaries — 24 October 2026:** [Correction and limits](../FLOATING-INTEGER-BOUNDARIES.md) reject the signed2⁶³/unsigned2⁶⁴ overflow thresholds and preserve accepted large unsigned magnitudes, with72 constructor/cast/reference/castable cases. Unsigned Decimal truncation and generic storage remain separate. Source1.25.1 unpublished/public1.25.0 accepted; REQ-126 partial. **Integer constructor/cast audit — 24 October 2026:** [Evidence and next correction](../INTEGER-CAST-AUDIT.md) add72 supported controls and150 observed diagnostics. Floating-point signed/unsigned boundaries silently admit out-of-range values; unsigned decimal truncation and generic storage/error policy are separate findings. No engine/version/release change. Adds34 source cases; current native Unix improves to22/2/0. Generic constructors/casts remain separate. General casts, unary/division and Unix-time wide conversion remain separate. Name and Classification **Timestamp deadlines — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:unix-dateTime](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-unix-dateTime), [fn:seconds](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-seconds), and [fn:duration-to-seconds](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-duration-to-seconds). Initial engine delivery: [PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84), [revision f7f55b4e](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19), REQ-118 4.0-S2. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. **Boundary review — 24 October 2026:** [Unix-time contract and current-draft comparison](../UNIX-DATETIME-CONTRACT.md) add52 source checks without changing the engine or the nonnegative frozen contract. Explicit current negative-epoch and wide-integer diagnostics remain unresolved; source/public1.25.0. Earlier source/public1.1.3 labels below are historical. ## 2. Intent Turn a receipt's epoch timestamp and measured processing time into UTC instants, then report elapsed and remaining seconds against a configured processing budget. Keep milliseconds and seconds explicit so the deadline is not scaled incorrectly. ## 3. Also Known As Epoch conversion and elapsed-budget accounting are descriptive terms. `seconds` constructs a duration; `seconds-from-duration` extracts a component and is not an alias for the total-seconds function. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 adds a scaled `xs:dayTimeDuration` to the UTC Unix epoch. Multiplying `PT1S` by a seconds count builds a duration, and dividing by `PT1S` gets its total seconds. The complete comparison returns the same report. Its epoch addition returns a dateTime; matching report text does not prove the same stamp subtype. ## 5. Motivation A receipt log often stores epoch milliseconds while service budgets use seconds. A 1,250-millisecond processing measurement is 1.25 seconds, not 1,250 seconds. A duration containing minutes also needs total seconds; taking just its seconds component would understate elapsed time. The report exposes both unit conversions. ## 6. Language Alignment `unix-dateTime` uses **nonnegative epoch milliseconds**, returning a UTC `xs:dateTimeStamp` in Bosak. Omitted or empty input means zero (the epoch), not the current time. A negative argument raises FOCA0002. Unix time assumes 86,400-second days and does not account for leap seconds. `seconds` accepts an optional decimal count, returning a day-time duration with fractional and negative values preserved. `duration-to-seconds` returns an optional decimal total for a day-time duration. Both return empty for empty input. For example PT1M30S has total 90 seconds but a seconds component of 30. Year-month durations cannot be converted to a fixed seconds count by this rule. ## 7. Applicability Use for explicit epoch-unit conversion and elapsed-budget reports from supplied measurements. The fixture assumes nonnegative integer epoch milliseconds, nonnegative elapsed milliseconds, and a nonnegative decimal seconds budget. Negative remaining time is allowed: it reports an overrun. These are measured values, not a clock read. The host owns monotonic measurement, actual cancellation and timeout enforcement; this XPath merely calculates a report. The supported Gregorian date range and decimal precision remain implementation limits. The examples do not establish unlimited timestamp or duration ranges. ## 8. Structure Convert receipt milliseconds to a received UTC instant. Divide measured milliseconds by 1,000 before building an elapsed duration. Build a budget duration directly from seconds. Add both to received time, subtract finished time from the deadline, and project total seconds for the report. ## 9. Participants The receipt supplies timestamp, elapsed measurement and budget with named units. The epoch converter creates the received instant. Duration functions normalize units. DateTime arithmetic derives finished/deadline instants. The comparison reports whether completion is within the budget. ## 10. Collaborations All instants use explicit UTC, avoiding implicit-timezone dependence. The report uses `$finished le $deadline`, so exact equality is within budget. Preserve signed remaining seconds to distinguish unused allowance from an overrun. ## 11. Consequences Fractional measurements survive the conversion. A negative remaining duration signals lateness without losing its magnitude. None of these functions sleeps, retries a request, cancels processing or checks the current wall clock. Calling `unix-dateTime()` always returns the epoch, which must not be mistaken for a receipt's missing timestamp. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Epoch milliseconds, omitted/empty zero and UTC subtype; Experimental signed epochs with frozen negative refusal; Duration total seconds, signs/fractions and bounded-calendar errors. **Boundaries:** Published wide-integer/range fixes are delivered; permissive scalar/cardinality conversion and bounded DateTimeOffset calendar remain separate. Follow-up groups: F01, F02, F08, F10. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Use `CompileOptions.Compatibility40` for the new calls. The default 3.1 profile rejects them; the comparison uses `Compatibility31`. The existing [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks exact reports/errors and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. All values are inline and deterministic; no external context or clock is needed. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Date/time review](../DATE-TIME-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed receipt-retention README](../examples/date-contracts/README.md) supply 108 checks across five families: keywords, Gregorian field sets, offsets, units, empty/default, precision and type/cardinality boundaries, plus complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. Malformed/multi-item tolerance, record conversion and fractional-component loss remain engine follow-ups. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits remain. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic receipt input: ```xml ``` [Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/timestamp-deadlines/main.xpath): ```xpath let $receipt := parse-xml('')/receipt let $received := unix-dateTime(xs:integer($receipt/@epochMilliseconds)) let $elapsed := seconds(xs:decimal($receipt/@elapsedMilliseconds) div 1000) let $budget := seconds(xs:decimal($receipt/@budgetSeconds)) let $finished := $received + $elapsed let $deadline := $received + $budget return concat('received=', $received, '; finished=', $finished, '; deadline=', $deadline, '; elapsedSeconds=', duration-to-seconds($elapsed), '; remainingSeconds=', duration-to-seconds($deadline - $finished), '; withinBudget=', $finished le $deadline) ``` Exact output: ```text received=2024-01-31T12:00:00Z; finished=2024-01-31T12:00:01.25Z; deadline=2024-01-31T12:00:02.5Z; elapsedSeconds=1.25; remainingSeconds=1.25; withinBudget=true ``` [Complete XPath 3.1 comparison](../examples/timestamp-deadlines/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $receipt := parse-xml('')/receipt return let $received := xs:dateTime('1970-01-01T00:00:00Z') + xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0.001S') * xs:integer($receipt/@epochMilliseconds) return let $elapsed := xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S') * (xs:decimal($receipt/@elapsedMilliseconds) div 1000) return let $budget := xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S') * xs:decimal($receipt/@budgetSeconds) return let $finished := $received + $elapsed return let $deadline := $received + $budget return concat('received=', $received, '; finished=', $finished, '; deadline=', $deadline, '; elapsedSeconds=', ($elapsed div xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S')), '; remainingSeconds=', (($deadline - $finished) div xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S')), '; withinBudget=', $finished le $deadline) ``` Exact output: ```text received=2024-01-31T12:00:00Z; finished=2024-01-31T12:00:01.25Z; deadline=2024-01-31T12:00:02.5Z; elapsedSeconds=1.25; remainingSeconds=1.25; withinBudget=true ``` ### Budget overrun Full input increases measured processing to three seconds: ```xml ``` The [over-budget expression](../examples/timestamp-deadlines/over-budget.xpath) reports: ```text received=2024-01-31T12:00:00Z; It does not run a timer or allocate a schedule. No benchmark is implied; decimal precision and the processor's supported date range bound representable values. ## 15. Known Uses This receipt-accounting scenario is synthetic. Existing evidence includes [`UnixDateTime_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`UnixDateTime_LargeTimestamp`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`UnixDateTime_NegativeValue_RaisesFoca0002`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Seconds_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Seconds_EmptySequence_ReturnsEmpty`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`DurationToSeconds_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`SecondsAndDurationToSeconds_AreInverses`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). There is no exact fn-seconds or fn-duration-to-seconds assignment: fn-seconds-from-duration/from-time are different functions. Named tests and these 17 examples provide separate evidence; no gate membership changes are included. The additional [`UnixDateTimeContractTests`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/UnixDateTimeContractTests.cs) verify `SupportedMilliseconds_AreExact`, `Default_IsEpochRatherThanNow`, `ResultTypeAndUtc_AreIndependentOfImplicitTimezone` and complete `DeadlineReport_MatchesXPath31Baseline` outcomes. Fresh full-set `fn-unix-dateTime` evidence and the four current-native failures are in the linked contract review; no gate promotion or new catalog-manifest cases are implied. ## 16. Related Features [Month-end cutoffs](month-end-cutoffs.md) covers Gregorian calendars and numeric offsets. [Bounded retry state](bounded-retries.md) uses finite attempt budgets. [The completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) tracks reference names and remaining coverage independently of exhaustive conformance.

sections.13:
Complete synthetic receipt input:

```xml
<receipt epochMilliseconds="1706702400000" elapsedMilliseconds="1250" budgetSeconds="2.5"/>
```

[Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/timestamp-deadlines/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $receipt := parse-xml('<receipt epochMilliseconds="1706702400000" elapsedMilliseconds="1250" budgetSeconds="2.5"/>')/receipt
let $received := unix-dateTime(xs:integer($receipt/@epochMilliseconds))
let $elapsed := seconds(xs:decimal($receipt/@elapsedMilliseconds) div 1000)
let $budget := seconds(xs:decimal($receipt/@budgetSeconds))
let $finished := $received + $elapsed
let $deadline := $received + $budget
return concat('received=', $received, '; finished=', $finished, '; deadline=', $deadline, '; elapsedSeconds=', duration-to-seconds($elapsed), '; remainingSeconds=', duration-to-seconds($deadline - $finished), '; withinBudget=', $finished le $deadline)
```

Exact output:

```text
received=2024-01-31T12:00:00Z; finished=2024-01-31T12:00:01.25Z; deadline=2024-01-31T12:00:02.5Z; elapsedSeconds=1.25; remainingSeconds=1.25; withinBudget=true
```

[Complete XPath 3.1 comparison](../examples/timestamp-deadlines/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $receipt := parse-xml('<receipt epochMilliseconds="1706702400000" elapsedMilliseconds="1250" budgetSeconds="2.5"/>')/receipt
return let $received := xs:dateTime('1970-01-01T00:00:00Z') + xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0.001S') * xs:integer($receipt/@epochMilliseconds)
return let $elapsed := xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S') * (xs:decimal($receipt/@elapsedMilliseconds) div 1000)
return let $budget := xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S') * xs:decimal($receipt/@budgetSeconds)
return let $finished := $received + $elapsed
return let $deadline := $received + $budget
return concat('received=', $received, '; finished=', $finished, '; deadline=', $deadline, '; elapsedSeconds=', ($elapsed div xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S')), '; remainingSeconds=', (($deadline - $finished) div xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S')), '; withinBudget=', $finished le $deadline)
```

Exact output:

```text
received=2024-01-31T12:00:00Z; finished=2024-01-31T12:00:01.25Z; deadline=2024-01-31T12:00:02.5Z; elapsedSeconds=1.25; remainingSeconds=1.25; withinBudget=true
```

### Budget overrun

<receipt epochMilliseconds="1706702400000" elapsedMilliseconds="3000" budgetSeconds="2.5"/>

Archive and partner URI policy

Frozen 4.0 — Boolean options and component precedence

## 1. Name and Classification **URI option policy — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:parse-uri](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-parse-uri) and [fn:build-uri](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-build-uri). Initial engine delivery: [PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84), [revision f7f55b4e](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19), REQ-118 4.0-S2. Definitions reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG function source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review does not recover the historical adopted specification snapshot. General syntax: [RFC 3986](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986) and [RFC 3987](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3987). ## 2. Intent Interpret a configured network archive as a UNC path and construct an invoice route from a partner endpoint. Choose structured components deliberately when legacy raw fields coexist. ## 3. Also Known As URI component policy and UNC interpretation are descriptive terms; no aliases are registered. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can assemble known routes from host-validated metadata. The comparison below uses separate server/folder/leaf and host attributes; it does not implement generic parsing, percent decoding, UNC detection or password filtering. ## 5. Motivation Archive paths and HTTP endpoints need different interpretation. A leading double slash normally denotes a relative authority; enabling UNC interpretation instead preserves the server/share text as a file path. Partner configuration may retain obsolete raw authority, path and query fields while a new structured route overrides them. ## 6. Language Alignment Compile with `XPathCompatibility.XPath40`. The runner refuses successful new-function fixtures in default 3.1 mode. Both functions accept an optional options map; empty options use defaults. Bosak registers keywords `uri`/`options` for parsing and `parts`/`options` for building. The working keyword fixture verifies the parser's actual metadata. | Option | Reviewed type/default | Effect | |---|---|---| | `allow-deprecated-features` | `xs:boolean`, `false()` | Retain nonempty password-bearing structured userinfo | | `omit-default-ports` | `xs:boolean`, `false()` | Omit recognized scheme-default structured ports | | `unc-path` | `xs:boolean`, `false()` | Interpret leading slashes as UNC when parsing; select the file prefix when building | Always supply Boolean values. Bosak currently applies effective Boolean value: the nonempty string `'false'` enables the tested options. These observed fixtures record a validation gap against the Boolean contract. ## 7. Applicability Use for configured archive paths and route assembly. Parsing does not validate a destination or perform network/file I/O. The synthetic `demo:placeholder` is example data. Password filtering is not redaction: the original URI and raw authority can retain the text. ## 8. Structure Parse archive with explicit UNC policy; parse partner with default-port omission; build a fresh route from host, scheme, segments and query map. Do not copy raw authority into the structured route. ## 9. Participants The route XML supplies configuration; component maps carry parsed values; `path-segments` preserves `INV/2048` as one encoded business identifier; the options map supplies Boolean policy. ## 10. Collaborations `parse-xml`, map lookup, `exists`, `concat` and `encode-for-uri` support the complete report and portable comparison. [Invoice API URIs](invoice-api-uris.md) explains decoding, repeated query keys and textual roundtrip limits. ## 11. Consequences Structured userinfo/host/port take precedence over raw authority when any is present. Otherwise raw authority is appended unchanged: password/default-port options do not inspect it, as stated by the reviewed draft. Nonempty segment sequences override raw path; an empty sequence falls back, while one empty string is a present segment and can produce an empty path. A nonempty query map overrides raw query. **Observed draft gap:** an empty map is still a present item under the reviewed rules, but Bosak falls back to raw query. Remove the raw query field when deliberately building with an empty query map. UNC construction uses a literal `:////` prefix after `file`. The tested leading path slash therefore yields `file://///server/share`; this is verified spelling, not a claim of canonical file-URI representation. Password-free userinfo with an empty password (`demo:`) is retained. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Boolean deprecated/default-port/UNC policies; Structured versus raw authority/path/query precedence; Nonmap option and malformed authority errors. **Boundaries:** String false currently enables a Boolean option; empty query map currently falls back to raw query. Raw-authority bypass itself is draft-defined. Follow-up groups: F01, F04. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. See [FunctionLibrary](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs): `UriBooleanOption`, `ParseUri` and `BuildUri`. The empty-query-map branch and option truthiness are observed implementation limits. Public function conversion rejects non-map options with `XPTY0004`, including empty parse input; unmatched bracket authority raises `FOUR0001`. No engine changes are included here. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** Keyword drift: implemented uri differs from pinned value; the [signature audit](../SIGNATURE-CONTRACT-AUDIT.md) publishes paired success/refusal files. Existing positional option-policy examples remain valid. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: ```xml ``` Complete [main fixture](../examples/uri-option-policy/main.xpath): ```xpath let $r := parse-xml('')/routes return let $archive := parse-uri(string($r/archive/@value), map {'unc-path': true()}) return let $api := parse-uri(string($r/partner/@value), map {'omit-default-ports': true()}) return let $target := build-uri(map {'scheme': $api?scheme, 'host': $api?host, 'port': $api?port, 'authority': 'ignored.example.test:8443', 'path': '/ignored', 'path-segments': ('', 'v2', 'invoices', 'INV/2048'), 'query': 'ignored=1', 'query-parameters': map {'status': 'ready now'}}) return concat('archive-scheme=', $archive?scheme, '; archive=', $archive?filepath, '; partner=', $target, '; userinfo=', exists($api?userinfo)) ``` Output: ```text archive-scheme=file; archive=//files.example.test/invoices/October 2026; partner=https://api.example.test/v2/invoices/INV%2F2048?status=ready%20now; userinfo=false ``` The archive has no parsed host component under UNC policy. Partner password-bearing userinfo is absent and port 443 is omitted; the freshly built route overrides deliberately conflicting raw fields. ### XPath 3.1 comparison Host-provided normalized archive metadata and validated HTTPS host allow this scoped construction: ```xpath let $r := parse-xml('')/routes return let $archive := concat('//', $r/archive/@server, '/', $r/archive/@folder, '/', $r/archive/@leaf) return let $target := concat('https://', $r/partner/@host, '/v2/invoices/', encode-for-uri('INV/2048'), '?status=', encode-for-uri('ready now')) return concat('archive=', $archive, '; partner=', $target) ``` Output: ```text archive=//files.example.test/invoices/October 2026; partner=https://api.example.test/v2/invoices/INV%2F2048?status=ready%20now ``` This comparison constructs the two addresses; it does not produce parsed scheme/userinfo evidence. Warehouse Pick Sorting

Retained sorting functions — portable workflow and 4.0 contract limits

## 1. Name and Classification [fn:sort](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-sort) and [array:sort](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-sort) are existing 3.1 functions retained in the 4.0 draft. They are outside the 117-name inventory of 4.0-only functions. Implementation reviewed at Bosak [source baseline 0597047a](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/0597047aed99851d10445993e2e636f3aeb437f2/src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs), with the named tests below. Historical adopted draft pins remain unavailable. Current review: 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG F&O source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). ## 2. Intent Produce a warehouse pick order by aisle and numeric bin, preserving input order for tied locations. Sort a sequence of XML lines and an array whose members contain both the original line and its quantity without separating that payload. ## 3. Also Known As Stable key sorting and lexicographic composite keys describe this workflow. There is no new function name or alias. ## 4. History / Supersedes The stable [3.1 sequence sort](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-sort) and [3.1 array sort](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-array-sort) already support a collation and a key callback. The reviewed 4.0 draft defines these compatibility functions through `sort-by`/`array:sort-by`, including the new numeric comparison rules. Retaining the function names does not make every numeric contract unchanged. The portable report below runs in both profiles. ## 5. Motivation Bin `10` should follow bin `2` within an aisle. Sorting raw bin text would put `10` before `2`. Equal-location lines must retain their original order, and quantities must travel with their corresponding lines. Explicit typed keys and member boundaries make those rules visible. ## 6. Language Alignment Both functions have one-, two- and three-argument forms. Omitted/empty collation uses the context default. An omitted key uses atomized input values. Explicit empty keys currently raise `XPTY0004` in the nonempty sequence/array probes, although the reviewed 4.0 draft defines default-on-empty. Supply `data#1` explicitly as a verified workaround; an empty key argument differs from a key callback that returns an empty sequence. A key can be a sequence: values are compared lexicographically, with the first differing position determining order. Equal complete keys preserve input order; an empty key precedes a nonempty key. The sequence callback receives one input item. The array callback receives a whole member, which can contain multiple items or be empty. Sorting rearranges members without flattening their payload. `array:append` deliberately creates one two-item member per line; an `array { ... }` constructor over a flat sequence would create different member boundaries. **Observed numeric gaps:** Bosak's retained functions use the shared `XdmValueComparer`, rather than the reviewed exact numeric ordering. Input `(3.1e0, 3.1)` remains double then decimal because promotion makes its keys tie; the reviewed 4.0 ordering puts decimal first. Both sequence and array probes record that limit. The two-item NaN probes also depend on input direction: `(NaN, 1)` produces number then NaN, while `(1, NaN)` produces NaN then number. The pinned numeric ordering places NaN below numbers. These are observed gaps, not a promised ordering policy for larger inputs. Corrected engine behavior must update the observed expectations while retaining historical migration notes. QName keys are refused in the demonstrated case. The reviewed sorting rules also exclude nonordered QName keys; broader `fn:compare` support does not authorize assuming every atomic family is a valid sort key. Bosak accepts the unknown-collation URI in both empty-input and nonempty-string probes; the latter returns codepoint-like order rather than `FOCH0002`. These results do not establish that the URI is supported. Use a known explicit collation and keep unknown-URI validation as an implementation follow-up. ## 7. Applicability This synthetic warehouse vocabulary assumes present IDs/aisles, valid integer bins and quantities, and a declared codepoint aisle policy. It omits route optimization, stock allocation, units, scheduling and locale-sensitive aisle names. Invalid bin text raises a constructor error. Production data should be validated before sorting, and NaN/mixed numeric keys need an explicit policy. ## 8. Structure Parse XML, construct an aisle/bin key, sort original lines, build an array of line/quantity members, and sort those members using the key from their first item. Render both orders for reconciliation. ## 9. Participants Lines carry locations and quantities. A key callback returns a string followed by an integer. The collation controls aisle strings. Array members bind each line to its converted quantity. Output projection preserves the sorted order. ## 10. Collaborations Use `string(@aisle)` and `xs:integer(@bin)` to state both key types. Compare corresponding key positions, not aisle strings against bin integers. Simple-map projection (`! string(@id)`) preserves the sequence's chosen order; a path over nodes can restore document order. The member callback accesses the line with `$member[1]`, and indexed output keeps its quantity alongside it. Lines C and D share a key and therefore remain in input order. ## 11. Consequences Both profiles produce C, D, B, A with quantities 3, 4, 1, 2. The workflow uses homogeneous types at each key position and avoids the observed mixed numeric and NaN gaps. Stable ties do not define a secondary business priority. An empty batch yields empty sequence/member reports, while an empty array member remains a member in the separate boundary probe. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Stable lexicographic keys with sequence items versus whole array members; Omitted versus explicit-empty keys and explicit data#1 workaround; Known collation, mixed-type errors, NaN and exact cross-numeric order. **Boundaries:** Explicit empty keys, unknown collations, NaN and promoted mixed-number ties remain unsupported draft contracts; use validated homogeneous keys. Follow-up groups: F05, F06. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. The report runs with either `CompileOptions.Compatibility40` or `CompileOptions.Compatibility31`. Keyword calls use 4.0 syntax and match the reviewed names `input`/`array`, `collation` and `key`. The explicit `sort-by` comparison verifies the illustrated sequence-key equivalence, not every draft contract or support for the draft's entire array-sort-by surface. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks `baselineExpected` for shared default-mode outcomes and `baselineError` for keyword refusal. Error cases verify diagnostic markers. Observed-limit fixtures preserve current evidence rather than certifying conformance. No engine or gate membership changes are made by this delivery. **Existing-function default review (2026-10-12):** The [ordering/default review](../ORDER-DEFAULT-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) and [detailed supplier README](../examples/order-contracts/README.md) add 132 checks across sort/array:sort/min/max/map:merge, explicit key/options and collation/NaN/cardinality boundaries, and six full 3.1/4.0 reports. Supplier price-plus-ID keys preserve business tie-breaking under source reordering. Use simple mapping to project sorted node IDs; a path restores document order. This is targeted evidence, not an engine fix or full D2 completion. ## 13. operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.m.text:
Destructuring let

Catalog entry — Operators & syntax · Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **Destructuring `let` bindings** — **Frozen 4.0** (ships at the `XPath40` level; static XPST0003 at `XPath31`). Spec: XPath 4.0 §4.14 (FLWOR expressions), [QT4CG PR #1131](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/pull/1131). Landed: REQ-123 destructuring-let cluster, [PR #129](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/129) (main `b8e4b9f`, 2026-10-10). **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: let expressions](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-let-expressions). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #129](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/129), [immutable mainline revision `b8e4b9f5`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/b8e4b9f510543c04d88a7c10ee2af28808a0fd5c) (2026-10-10). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Bind several variables at once by decomposing a sequence, an array, or a map on the right-hand side — `let $($x, $y) := (1, 2)` binds `$x` to `1` and `$y` to `2` in one clause, evaluating the right-hand side exactly once. ## 3. Also Known As "Destructuring binding" (spec), "tuple binding" (informal, from the tuple-builder relative). Not to be confused with the `for` clause's *tuple* destructuring, which is a separate (larger) construct. ## 4. History / Supersedes Supersedes three 3.1 idioms, one per container kind: | Before (3.1) | After (4.0) | |---|---| | `let $x := $seq[1] let $y := $seq[2] return …` — repeated positional indexing, RHS re-evaluated per binding if not manually cached | `let $($x, $y) := $seq return …` — one evaluation, positional bind | | `let $a := $arr(1) let $b := $arr(2) return …` | `let $[$a, $b] := $arr return …` | | `let $n := map:get($m, "name") let $a := map:get($m, "addr") return …` | `let ${$name, $addr} := $m return …` — keys are the variable local names | ## 5. Motivation The 3.1 idioms are error-prone in two ways: the RHS is visually repeated (or manually hoisted into a helper variable, cluttering scope), and positional indexing silently does the wrong thing when the sequence is shorter than expected. Destructuring makes the arity contract explicit and puts the shape of the data next to the names it feeds. ## 6. Language Alignment Prior art: ML/Haskell pattern bindings, ES6 `const {a, b} = obj` / `const [x, y] = arr`. **Semantic drift — read before relying on intuition:** - The **last variable of a sequence pattern takes all remaining items** (`let $($x, $y) := (1,2,3)` → `$y = (2,3)`); ES6 array destructuring instead discards surplus elements. Surplus *variables* (too few items) bind `()`. - The **array form discards surplus members but requires each bound index**: `let $[$a, $b] := [1,2,3]` discards member 3, but too few members for the variables is **FOAY0001**, not `undefined`-style filling. - The **map form binds by variable name** (`${$name}` looks up key `"name"`), closer to ES6 object destructuring than to map lookup — but a missing key binds `()` rather than throwing. ## 7. Applicability Use for: unpacking fixed-shape sequences/arrays/maps at the head of a FLWOR; replacing two-or-more positional `let`s over the same value. Do **not** use for: library expressions that must still compile at `XPath31` (static XPST0003); one-item unpacks (`let $x := $seq[1]` remains clearer); hot loops where the save/restore cost (§14) matters and the 3.1 form was already hoisted. ## 8. Structure ``` LetBinding ::= SimpleLetBinding | DestructuringLetBinding DestructuringLetBinding ::= "$" ("(" | "[" | "{") VariableSpec ("," VariableSpec)* (")" | "]" | "}") TypeDeclaration? ":=" ExprSingle VariableSpec ::= "$" VarName (TypeDeclaration)? (* per-variable type, optional *) ``` Three bracket kinds select the source container: `(` sequence, `[` single array, `{` single map. ## 9. Participants - `XPathParser.ParseDestructuringLetBinding` — parses all three kinds; gated on the parser's xpath40 flag; empty pattern → XPST0003. - `XPathAstNode.LetDestructuringKind`, `DestructuringVariable` — AST model. - Opcodes `Destructure`, `SaveVariables`, `RestoreVariables` (`IrOpCode` 1.12) — binding extraction and lexical scoping, lowered by `IrLowerer` (1.54). - `VmEngine` (2.173/2.174) — `Destructure` semantics, `EnforceType` §3.4.2 coercion, `TryRelabelToDerivedNumeric` (PR 254 relabeling). - `EvaluationContext.TryGetDirectVariable` (2.36) — direct-binding probe for `SaveVariables`. ## 10. Collaborations - **Typed simple lets** (`let $v as xs:T := e`) — parsed at XP40+ as part of this slice; `EnforceType` applies XPath 4.0 §3.4.2 coercion when `IsXPath40` (untypedAtomic cast, numeric promotion, record coercion, derived-integer relabeling). - **Structural record types** — a `map(K,V)`/`record(...)` whole-pattern type validates the RHS shape (record patterns reject undeclared variables). - **Lexical scoping** — `SaveVariables`/`RestoreVariables` wrap every `LetExpression` binding group; a trailing reference to a destructured variable outside the let's body raises XPST0008. (Caveat: emitted for `LetExpression` bindings only; XQuery full-FLWOR scoping has its own machinery.) ## 11. Consequences Benefits: single RHS evaluation; arity made explicit; map unpacks name their keys at the binding site. Liabilities: three binding semantics to learn (sequence rest / array strictness / map-by-name) — the drift table in §6 is the cheat sheet. Relabeling changes the *annotation*, not the datum (`42` → `xs:short` ✓; `2.5` → `xs:integer` is XPTY0004, never truncation). Save/Restore pairs are exception-unsafe by design (abandoned evaluations discard the frame with the whole stack — intentional). ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers REQ123-destructuring. Sequence rest/short inputs, array member groups/surplus/short errors, map missing keys, per-variable/whole-pattern types, duplicates and lexical shadowing are mapped. Undeclared annotated-record fields incorrectly bind empty when destructured. K03 retains the required record-lookup XPTY0004 expectation. Plain-map missing-key emptiness remains a different supported contract. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. Files: `src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs` (1.74), `src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathAstNode.cs` (1.25), `src/Bosak.XPath.Compiler/Ir/IrOpCode.cs` (1.12), `src/Bosak.XPath.Compiler/Ir/IrLowerer.cs` (1.54), `src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs` (2.173/2.174), `src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/EvaluationContext.cs` (2.36). Version gate: XPST0003 at `XPath31`; fully legal at `XPath40`. Regression: `VersionGateTests` (0.20, +10 rows), `ParserTests` (0.11, +6 AST tests). ## 13. Sample Code Additional executable catalog cases unpack invoice metadata and explicitly test a missing currency key: [main](../examples/destructuring-let/main.xpath) produces `INV-1042 / EUR`; [edge](../examples/destructuring-let/edge.xpath) returns missing currency cardinality `0`. These run at `XPath40` and verify default-mode refusal. Start with [the invoice chapter's practical migration pair](../worked-examples/invoice-to-erp/README.md#where-xpath-40-can-improve-readability): unpack invoice ID and currency from a metadata map to build a display label. Both complete expressions are supplied, engine-verified, and produce `INV-2026-1042 / EUR`. The 4.0 form requires explicit opt-in. The probes below cover the individual binding shapes. ~~~xquery let $($x, $y) := (1, 2, 3) return ($x, $y) (: → (1, (2,3)) — last variable takes the rest :) let $[$a, $b] := [3, 4, 5] return `a={$a} b={$b}` (: → "a=3 b=4" — surplus member 5 discarded :) let $[$a, $b] := [1] return $b (: → FOAY0001 :) let ${$name} := map {"name": "Braid"} return $name (: → "Braid" — key = variable local name :) let $($x as xs:short, $y) := (42, "ok") return ($x, $y) (: → (42 xs:short, "ok") — PR 254 relabeling; annotation changes, datum untouched :) ~~~ ## 14. Performance Notes Cost class: **small constant overhead**. One `Destructure` opcode per binding group plus one `SaveVariables`/`RestoreVariables` frame pair — no per-item re-evaluation (the 3.1 un-hoisted idiom this replaces was potentially *more* expensive). No hot-path interaction known. No BenchmarkDotNet measurement exists for this feature as of 2026-10-10; the cost class is an implementation expectation, not a measurement. ## 15. Known Uses Practical case: `InvoiceReferenceGuideTests.InvoiceLabel_MigrationPairMatchesAndRequiresOptIn` executes both published label expressions and verifies XPST0003 in the default mode. sections.2: Bind several variables at once by decomposing a sequence, an array, or a map on the right-hand side — `let $($x, $y) := (1, 2)` binds `$x` to `1` and `$y` to `2` in one clause, evaluating the right-hand side exactly once.
sections.3: "Destructuring binding" (spec), "tuple binding" (informal, from the tuple-builder relative). Not to be confused with the `for` clause's *tuple* destructuring, which is a separate (larger) construct.
sections.4:
Supersedes three 3.1 idioms, one per container kind:

| Before (3.1) | After (4.0) |
|---|---|
| `let $x := $seq[1] let $y := $seq[2] return …` — repeated positional indexing, RHS re-evaluated per binding if not manually cached | `let $($x, $y) := $seq return …` — one evaluation, positional bind |
| `let $a := $arr(1) let $b := $arr(2) return …` | `let $[$a, $b] := $arr return …` |
| `let $n := map:get($m, "name") let $a := map:get($m, "addr") return …` | `let ${$name, $addr} := $m return …` — keys are the variable local names |
sections.5: The 3.1 idioms are error-prone in two ways: the RHS is visually repeated (or manually hoisted into a helper variable, cluttering scope), and positional indexing silently does the wrong thing when the sequence is shorter than expected. Destructuring makes the arity contract explicit and puts the shape of the data next to the names it feeds.
sections.6:
Prior art: ML/Haskell pattern bindings, ES6 `const {a, b} = obj` / `const [x, y] = arr`.

**Semantic drift — read before relying on intuition:**

- The **last variable of a sequence pattern takes all remaining items** (`let $($x, $y) := (1,2,3)` → `$y = (2,3)`); ES6 array destructuring instead discards surplus elements. Surplus *variables* (too few items) bind `()`.
- The **array form discards surplus members but requires each bound index**: `let $[$a, $b] := [1,2,3]` discards member 3, but too few members for the variables is **FOAY0001**, not `undefined`-style filling.
- The **map form binds by variable name** (`${$name}` looks up key `"name"`), closer to ES6 object destructuring than to map lookup — but a missing key binds `()` rather than throwing.
sections.7:
Use for: unpacking fixed-shape sequences/arrays/maps at the head of a FLWOR; replacing two-or-more positional `let`s over the same value.

Do **not** use for: library expressions that must still compile at `XPath31` (static XPST0003); one-item unpacks (`let $x := $seq[1]` remains clearer); hot loops where the save/restore cost (§14) matters and the 3.1 form was already hoisted.
sections.8:
```
LetBinding ::= SimpleLetBinding | DestructuringLetBinding
DestructuringLetBinding ::= "$" ("(" | "[" | "{") VariableSpec ("," VariableSpec)* (")" | "]" | "}")
                            TypeDeclaration? ":=" ExprSingle
VariableSpec ::= "$" VarName (TypeDeclaration)?        (* per-variable type, optional *)
```

Three bracket kinds select the source container: `(` sequence, `[` single array, `{` single map.

Benefits: single RHS evaluation; arity made explicit; map unpacks name their keys at the binding site.

Focus-function syntax and pipeline focus

Frozen XPath 4.0 - bounded executable reference

## 1. Name and Classification **Focus-function syntax** - **Frozen 4.0**, REQ-118 S4. `fn { E }` and `function { E }` omit the signature and take one `item()*` argument, bound as the whole context value. `fn($x) { E }` abbreviates an ordinary explicit-signature inline function; it is not a focus function. This entry is distinct from the [zero-argument focus constructors](focus-functions.md). Delivery: [PR #87](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/87), immutable `ec79355936a29ac70eeea3ae47e4c4e2ee00d813`; that revision already contains the named focus-function tests. Current review: [immutable draft expressions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/xquery-40/src/expressions.xml), sections `id-inline-func`, `id-focus-functions`, `id-pipeline-operator`, and [InlineFunctionExpr grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/grammar-40/xpath-grammar.xml). Upstream master was refreshed on 22 October 2026. This is a current comparison pin, not recovery of a historically adopted specification revision. Source 1.23.5 remains unpublished; public 1.23.4 already contains this bounded syntax. ## 2. Intent Write a callback whose argument supplies its context value, and distinguish per-item processing from whole-sequence reduction. ## 3. Also Known As A focus function is an inline function without an explicit signature. Both `fn { ... }` and `function { ... }` are supplied forms. The keyword abbreviation `fn($x) { ... }` still has an explicit parameter list. A zero-argument constructor such as `xs:integer()` is a different feature. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, write `function($line as element()) { xs:decimal($line/@qty) * xs:decimal($line/@unit) }`. The paired [3.0 stylesheet](../examples/focus-function-syntax/report-3.xsl) and [4.0 stylesheet](../examples/focus-function-syntax/report-4.xsl) produce the same order-line report. A parameterized 3.1 function does not implicitly bind its parameter as the focus; references use `$line` explicitly. ## 5. Motivation An order feed contains line quantity and unit amount. The report computes one amount per line, preserves source line order, then reports the count and total over all amounts. A focus callback keeps the attribute calculation readable; the pipeline makes the whole-sequence summary distinct from the mapping stage. [The complete task and fixtures](../examples/focus-function-syntax/README.md) state assumptions, exact input/output and failure behavior. ## 6. Language Alignment This is XPath focus, not ambient JavaScript `this` or an implicit item-by-item lambda. The callback receives a sequence as a single argument and sets position/size to 1/1, even for an empty or multiple-item argument. `=!>` calls its target per input item; `->` evaluates its right expression once with the complete left value as context. The 3.1 `=>` arrow inserts a first function argument; it does not establish the pipeline context. Similar results for a unary example do not make these operators interchangeable. ## 7. Applicability Use a focus function for an attribute-oriented callback or a whole-value operation when its context contract is clear. Use explicit parameters when argument names/types improve clarity or caller position must be passed explicitly. In the report each amount callback receives exactly one line node. Empty input makes no mapping calls; the summary pipeline still runs once with an empty value. ## 8. Structure ```xpath fn { concat(count(.), ':', position(), ':', last()) }((9,8)) ``` This returns `2:1:1`. The runnable [whole-focus probe](../examples/focus-function-syntax/probes/whole-focus.xpath) returns `2:1:1` (count:position:size), and [empty-focus probe](../examples/focus-function-syntax/probes/empty-focus.xpath) returns `0:1:1`. ## 9. Participants [XPathParser.ParseInlineFunction](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) lowers an omitted signature into a single synthetic parameter plus a PipelineExprNode. [IrLowerer](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Compiler/Ir/IrLowerer.cs) and [VmEngine](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs) execute the existing function/focus path. Public callers use XPath31Expression/CompileOptions or ordinary XSLT stylesheets; no new API is introduced. ## 10. Collaborations The report's `$amount` focus function reads the supplied line; `$format` uses the explicit `fn(...)` abbreviation and typed named arguments; the per-item label callback captures those variables. Mapping creates line labels and amounts. The pipeline consumes the amounts as one value for count and sum. Caller focus is restored after inner calls/pipelines, as verified by named probes. ## 11. Consequences A callback argument containing two items is not two calls. A callback invoked from a simple map sees its own position/size 1/1, not the caller's 1/N, 2/N positions. An axis such as `@qty` requires an appropriate node context; the implicit signature alone does not validate the report's line schema. Wrong lexical decimals raise FORG0001 in both report versions. Values are formatted to two display decimals, without claiming a general accounting model. ## 12. Implementation **C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S4-focus. Pipeline whole-value/fixed-focus, focus-function implicit/explicit signatures, lexical capture/restoration and accepted mapping syntax are mapped. Mapping arrow extra arguments incorrectly see mapped-item focus rather than the containing focus. Use for $u in ... return F($u,A...) when extra arguments depend on outer dot/position/size. C03 constructor capture/type coverage remains distinct. Host/profile propagation belongs to C06. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance. Thirty new manifest cases use the existing CatalogExampleTests public execution path: 18 focused values/grammar/focus probes, four explicit 3.1 refusals and eight complete stylesheet reports. Sixteen successful XPath cases also assert a 3.1 refusal; two compatible forms retain baseline results. No engine, test runner, compatibility level or gate is changed. The reports use the default Legacy host with effective stylesheet versions 3.0/4.0, not an exhaustive host/module/package matrix. ## 13. Sample Code Input: ``. Both complete stylesheets yield `BOLT=25.00|NUT=10.00|FREE=0.00|lines=3;total=35.00`. Empty input yields `lines=0;total=0.00`; reordered input changes label order while retaining count/total. An invalid quantity `oops` raises FORG0001. [Full examples](../examples/focus-function-syntax/README.md) include every fixture, expected result, context and runnable file. ## 14. Performance Notes The report makes a bounded number of passes over N lines/amounts and emits O(N) labels. Function items and sequence materialization may allocate; no speed or memory advantage over the baseline is claimed. Use the benchmark harness for measured claims. Focus functions do not make the report streaming or parallel. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable evidence under the owner-approved AC-03 policy: `focus-syntax-report-3-normal`, `focus-syntax-report-4-normal`, their empty/reordered/invalid counterparts, and the `focus-syntax-*` probes in [the manifest](../examples/cases.json), executed by [CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs). All 30 case IDs and receipt hashes are recorded in [the slice audit](../FOCUS-FUNCTION-SYNTAX.json). Named existing tests in [VersionGateTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs): `Compile_FocusFunction_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_SpecExamples`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_BindsArgumentAsWholeContextValue`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_AfterMappingArrow`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_WrongArityThrows`, `Evaluate_Pipeline_SetsFixedFocusPositionOneSizeOne`, `Evaluate_Pipeline_FocusRestoredAfterEvaluation`. **No feature-specific qt4 gated-set assignment is made here**; named engine tests and runnable public examples are the explicit evidence. This does not assert that upstream lacks broader tests or claim whole-set conformance. The policy amendment does not automatically close acceptance of this or other entries. ## 16. Related Features [Pipeline](pipeline-operator.md), [mapping arrow](mapping-arrow.md), [zero-argument focus constructors](focus-functions.md), [keyword arguments](keyword-arguments.md), [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). Record casts/coercion/updates remain the next separate D3 scope.

Method-Call Operator =?>

Catalog entry — Operators & syntax · Deferred

**C07 lifecycle review — 26 October 2026:** [Current disposition and correction receipts](../LIFECYCLE-RECONCILIATION.md) distinguish delivered scope, retained history and pending acceptance. Six closure workpackages remain; no feature or profile promotion. ## 1. Name and Classification **Method-call operator `=?>`** — **Deferred** (deliberately not implemented). Spec: XPath 4.0 §4.22.3 (operator summary), [QT4CG issue #2219](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/issues/2219). Deferral recorded: REQ-118 dossier §1.2 "Still moving — do NOT build yet" (semantics changed 25 June 2026). **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: methods and method calls](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-methods). This is the adoption/disposition dossier delivery, not implementation of the refused shape. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Object-style method invocation on a value: the right-hand name is resolved against a method dictionary for the *type* of the left-hand value, so `$value =?> method(args)` dispatches to the method registered for that type rather than a plain in-scope function. ## 3. Also Known As "Method lookup operator". (No renames on record — the issue is semantic churn, not naming.) ## 4. History / Supersedes None — new capability; there is no 3.x idiom it replaces. The nearest 3.1/4.0 workaround it would relieve: | Before | After (if landed) | |---|---| | `map:get($m, "key")`, `array:get($a, 1)` — per-type function names a user must know | `$m =?> get("key")` — one call syntax, type-driven dispatch | ## 5. Motivation Type-directed dispatch would let maps, arrays, and future extensible types share call syntax, easing the "which module owns this operation?" burden. It is also the gateway shape for any future extensible-type story. ## 6. Language Alignment Prior art: Smalltalk/Objective-C message send, C# extension-method invocation syntax, Kotlin receiver types. Drift watch: XPath would dispatch on the **XDM type + registered method dictionary**, not on object identity or inheritance — and the *exact* resolution rules (what happens for unions, for `item()`, for user-defined types) are the part the WG changed in June 2026. ## 7. Applicability Not applicable — Bosak does not implement this operator. This entry exists so the deferral is a recorded decision rather than an absence. ## 8. Structure Not recorded — the grammar shape is among the things the draft may still adjust. Re-derive from the current WG Review Draft before any implementation attempt. ## 9. Participants None in Bosak. Implementation seam when the time comes: parser operator table, `ApplyBinaryOperator` dispatch in `VmEngine`, and interaction with the type-matching machinery used by `instance of` / `typeswitch`. ## 10. Collaborations Any future design would interact with delivered choice types, existing function lookup and bounded XSLT-defined nominative records. Their delivery does not implement method dispatch; full nominal declaration/model contracts remain separately limited. ## 11. Consequences Deferral leaves the operator unavailable. Consumers can use the supplied direct `map:*`/`array:*` alternatives; refusal and alternative checks remain necessary. Their passing results do not implement method dispatch or certify every possible replacement. ## 12. Implementation No implementation is adopted. The C07 probes verify `XPST0003` in XPath30, XPath31, XPath40 and XPath40Experimental. Any future implementation or tier decision requires a separately scoped review; this disposition makes no promotion commitment. ## 13. Sample Code No method-call syntax is committed. Do not cargo-cult `$x =?> f()` from draft-era blog posts. Use a verified stable alternative for a packing-plan array: [main.xpath](../examples/method-call-alternative/main.xpath) evaluates `array:size(['FILTER-A', 'BOLT-M8'])` to `2`; the [empty-array case](../examples/method-call-alternative/edge.xpath) returns `0`. Design note for the future: type-dictionary dispatch would add a per-call dictionary probe on the hot path — measure against the direct-function-call baseline in `benchmarks/Bosak.Benchmarks` before promoting out of experimental. ## 15. Known Uses No implementation evidence for the deferred operator is claimed. Published stable alternatives are `method-call-alternative-main` and `method-call-alternative-edge` in `CatalogExampleTests`. These checks do not promote or implement method-call syntax. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_MappingArrow_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_MappingArrow_AppliesFunctionPerItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_MappingArrow_WithArgumentsPrependsContextItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Decision record, not an engine delivery or a qt4 set promotion. Tests below pin the supported/refused alternatives. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features - [mapping-arrow-gtgt.md](../rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md) — the `=`-family rename history (`=>>` → `=!>`); if `=?>` ever ships, its name is the one stable thing about it so far. - `fn:scan` ([experimental/fn-scan.md](../experimental/fn-scan.md)) — an example of a separately adopted Experimental feature. Its adoption does not supersede the recorded method-call deferral or determine a future implementation tier. *Entry created 2026-10-10 (REQ-126 scaffold). operators-and-syntax/numeric-literals.md.text:
Numeric literals and digit separators

Frozen XPath 4.0 - bounded executable reference

**Public1.23.7 - 23 October2026:** EQName bracket parsing, inline-record signature gates and numeric separator boundaries are [published and verified](../../RELEASE-1.23.7-PUBLICATION.md). Current catalog74 entries/2,893 documentation checks; REQ-126/AC-03 remain partial. Braid dependency1.23.4 unchanged. Earlier source/unpublished checkpoints below are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Hexadecimal/binary integer literals and underscore separators** - **Frozen 4.0**, REQ-118 S3. Lowercase `0x` and `0b` introduce integer literals. Separators are permitted inside decimal, hexadecimal and binary digit groups, including the fraction and exponent groups of decimal/double literals. Ordinary XPath 3.0/3.1 syntax remains available; these extensions require 4.0. Current comparison: [immutable grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/grammar-40/xpath-grammar.xml), productions NumericLiteral, HexIntegerLiteral, BinaryIntegerLiteral, DecimalLiteral, DoubleLiteral, Digits, HexDigits and BinaryDigits. Upstream master was refreshed on 23 October 2026 at this revision. It is a current comparison pin, not a recovered historical adoption pin. [Delivery audit](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.md) separates the existing syntax from the source1.23.7 boundary correction; public release remains1.23.4. ## 2. Intent Make a bit mask or a large threshold readable in source code while retaining the numeric value and ordinary arithmetic semantics. ## 3. Also Known As Based integer literals; digit separators. `0xFF` is an integer, not an xs:hexBinary byte value. Binary literals are numbers, not xs:base64Binary values. Uppercase hex digits are accepted; uppercase prefixes `0X` and `0B` are refused. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1 use decimal `255` instead of `0xFF`, `4` instead of `0b0100`, and `1000` instead of `1_000`. The paired [3.0 stylesheet](../examples/numeric-literals/report-3.xsl) and [4.0 stylesheet](../examples/numeric-literals/report-4.xsl) keep the same telemetry report algorithm; only the constants change. Literals do not introduce a new runtime numeric type or relax input casting. ## 5. Motivation A telemetry feed stores flags and counts as decimal attributes. A report selects readings with bit 4 set and count at least 1000. The mask is easier to inspect in binary and the threshold easier to read with grouping. The [complete task](../examples/numeric-literals/README.md) includes normal, empty, reordered and invalid inputs and exact output. ## 6. Language Alignment The prefixes resemble C-family source literals; the exact XPath grammar governs the boundaries. Repeated internal underscores such as `1__000` and `0xFF__FF` are valid under the pinned draft. Each nonempty digit group starts and ends in a digit: `1._2`, `1.2_` and `1e_2` are invalid. A sign is a unary operator, not part of the integer token. Source separators do not extend the XML Schema lexical forms accepted by xs:integer: `xs:integer('1_000')` and `xs:integer('0xFF')` still fail FORG0001. ## 7. Applicability Use these constants in authored XPath/XSLT 4.0 expressions. Keep external decimal attributes in their declared lexical format, and select a 3.0/3.1-compatible spelling when generating an older stylesheet. This entry verifies ordinary Legacy-host effective3.0/4.0 stylesheets, not every package, XQuery or host override context. ## 8. Structure ```xpath 0xFF + 0b1_000 + 1_000 ``` The sum is1263. `1_2.3__4` is decimal12.34; `1_2.5e+0_2` is double1250. A decimal point may have no following digits (`1_2.`), and a decimal may omit its integer part (`.1_2`). If a fraction/exponent group is present, its separators cannot be at an edge. ## 9. Participants [XPathLexer](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Lexer/XPathLexer.cs) scans version-sensitive numeric tokens. [XPathParser](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) removes separators and computes based integer values. The public XPath31Expression/CompileOptions surface selects the compatibility level. No new public API is added. ## 10. Collaborations In the report the binary constant and hexadecimal zero form the mask; idiv/mod test the flag arithmetically. A separated threshold filters counts. xsl:for-each preserves input order, and sum builds the total from parsed decimal attribute values. The literals do not implement bitwise operators or alter data conversion. ## 11. Consequences The supplied checks cover integer/decimal/double identity, a value above Int64 range, negative unary application, numeric map/array lookup keys, valid internal repeated separators, malformed groups, wrong radix digits and version refusals. Bosak uses bounded .NET numeric representations; one above-Int64 example does not certify arbitrary-precision integer/decimal support. Other numeric adjacency, Unicode digit and overflow behavior is outside this bounded correction. No performance improvement is claimed. ## 12. Implementation **C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S3-lexical. Radix/separator token boundaries, template escaping/nesting/comment/atomization and old-profile/static-error cases are mapped. C03 retains numeric representation limits. Do not infer arbitrary precision, every adjacency/Unicode digit case, XML/XQuery string constructors or AVT/host behavior from these lexical probes. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance. **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies 4.0 radix/separator syntax and lower-profile refusal; Above-Int64 integer literals versus generic constructors/casts; Delivered floating thresholds, unsigned truncation and preserved integer identity. **Boundary:** A decimal-backed wide literal does not establish arbitrary precision or a matching generic constructor range. Generic wide xs:integer casts still narrow; .NET decimal precision remains bounded. Ownership: T01, T02. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. Fifty new catalog cases use the existing public CatalogExampleTests execution path. Initial38 probes produced30 passes and8 failures: malformed fractional/exponent underscore groups were accepted. Source1.23.7 rejects those groups only in the 4.0 lexer path. Thirty-four dedicated API cases cover those eight shapes in all four compatibility levels and valid-group controls in both4.0 profiles. Expected outcomes were not weakened. [Audit and retained evidence](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.md). ## 13. Sample Code The complete [4.0 report](../examples/numeric-literals/report-4.xsl) reads [normal.xml](../examples/numeric-literals/normal.xml): readings A(flags5,count1500), B(flags2,count900). It emits `A:ready|B:hold|ready=1;total=2400`, matching the3.0 baseline. Empty input emits `ready=0;total=0`; reordering changes row order; invalid count `oops` raises FORG0001. [Task and all expectations](../examples/numeric-literals/README.md) describe every instruction and input assumption. ## 14. Performance Notes Digit separators are removed during compilation; based integers are accumulated in the parser. These facts are implementation descriptions, not allocation or timing measurements. Report arithmetic and numeric conversion still run per reading. No benchmark or asymptotic improvement over decimal constants is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable AC-03 evidence: `numeric-literals-hex`, `numeric-literals-binary`, `numeric-literals-fraction`, `numeric-literals-exponent`, `numeric-literals-beyond-long`, `numeric-literals-invalid-13` and `numeric-literals-report-4-normal`, enumerated with all fifty cases in [the audit](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.json) and [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Named [NumericLiteralBoundaryTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/NumericLiteralBoundaryTests.cs) methods Compile_InvalidDigitGroup_ThrowsXpst0003 and Evaluate_ValidDigitGroups_ReturnExpectedValues independently cover the correction. Existing [VersionGateTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) methods Evaluate_HexBinaryLiterals_XPath40Mode_Work, Evaluate_UnderscoreSeparators_XPath40Mode_Work and Evaluate_HexBinaryLiterals_31Mode_ThrowXpst0003 remain relevant. Feature-specific qt4 assignment is explicitly unassigned in this slice; running the unchanged global gate does not establish individual production coverage or promote a set. ## 16. Related Features [String templates](string-templates.md), [keyword arguments](keyword-arguments.md), [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). The [grammar matrix](../GRAMMAR-COVERAGE-MATRIX.json) retains remaining host/declaration coverage. REQ-126 and D2/D3/D4/AC-03 remain partial.

```xpath
0xFF + 0b1_000 + 1_000
```

sections.10: In the report the binary constant and hexadecimal zero form the mask; idiv/mod test the flag arithmetically. A separated threshold filters counts. xsl:for-each preserves input order, and sum builds the total from parsed decimal attribute values. The literals do not implement bitwise operators or alter data conversion.

Motivation Process parcels or inventory updates spread across several arrays or maps. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Deferred/rejected contracts require explicit alternatives; they must not be advertised as implemented. ## 8. rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md.text:
Mapping Arrow =>> (Original Spelling)

Catalog entry — Rejected / Superseded

## 1. Name and Classification **Mapping arrow, original spelling `=>>`** — **Rejected–Superseded**. Bosak never shipped this spelling; the engine implemented the renamed form directly. Disposition recorded: REQ-118 dossier §1.2 "Deliberately rejected / renamed (do not implement old shapes)". **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: accepted mapping-arrow syntax](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-mapping-arrow-expression). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #77](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/77), [immutable mainline revision `27bc663b`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/27bc663b71b948318f69ee1f23173ac63046a525) (2026-10-08). This is the adoption/disposition dossier delivery, not implementation of the refused shape. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent (Of the accepted feature this spelling belonged to.) Apply the function once per item, passing that item as its first argument: `$seq =!> f()` corresponds to `for $x in $seq return f($x)`. The ordinary arrow `$seq => f()` passes the whole sequence as one argument. The simple map operator `!` instead establishes each item as the context for its right-hand expression; argument passing and context binding are distinct mechanisms. ## 3. Also Known As `=!>` — the accepted name (mapping arrow). Formerly spelled `=>>` in earlier drafts; renamed during draft stabilization. qt4tests pin the accepted spelling. ## 4. History / Supersedes The rejected spelling and its replacement are recorded in the REQ-118 audit; Bosak implements the accepted form in its S4 grammar slice. A 3.1 baseline uses `for $x in $seq return f($x)`. See the [accepted mapping-arrow entry](../operators-and-syntax/mapping-arrow.md) for the verified migration pair. The current specification link documents the accepted syntax; an exact historical rename revision remains part of the provenance work. ## 5. Motivation Recorded for completeness: the superseded spelling exists in draft-era examples, conference slides, and early blog posts. A user pasting such material gets a parse error and deserves a searchable answer. ## 6. Language Alignment The accepted operator performs per-item function application, comparable in purpose to mapping a collection. XPath passes each item as the first function argument; it does not establish that item as the right-hand expression's context in the way `!` does. The historical reason for choosing the replacement spelling needs its own source; no visual resemblance to other operators establishes it. ## 7. Applicability **Do not use.** `=>>` raises XPST0003 at every Bosak compatibility level, including frozen `XPath40`. Use `=!>`. ## 8. Structure Not applicable — the spelling is not in the grammar. Accepted form: `Expr "=!>" ArrowFunction`. ## 9. Participants None. The parser's operator table has no `=>>` token; drafts-era sources parse-fail positionally at the `>`. ## 10. Collaborations None. ## 11. Consequences Of the rejection: zero engine surface for the old spelling, one parse-error class for pasted old material, and no version-gate complexity (there is no "compat level that accepts `=>>`"). ## 12. Implementation None, deliberately. If a parser change ever accidentally accepts `=>>`, that is a defect against this entry. ## 13. Sample Code ~~~xquery string-join((' FILTER-A ', ' BOLT-M8 ') =!> normalize-space(), ',') (: → "FILTER-A,BOLT-M8" — one call per product code :) (' FILTER-A ') =>> normalize-space() (: → XPST0003 at every level — old spelling, never implemented :) ~~~ ## 14. Performance Notes Not applicable. ## 15. Known Uses `rejected-mapping-arrow-main` and `rejected-mapping-arrow-edge` in `CatalogExampleTests` verify an accepted product-code normalization and rejection of the old spelling. See [the accepted mapping-arrow case](../operators-and-syntax/mapping-arrow.md) and [complete rejection file](../examples/rejected-mapping-arrow/edge.xpath). qt4tests pin only the accepted `=!>` spelling (part of the frozen gate's grammar slices). No test uses `=>>`. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_MappingArrow_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_MappingArrow_AppliesFunctionPerItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_MappingArrow_WithArgumentsPrependsContextItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Decision record, not an engine delivery or a qt4 set promotion. Tests below pin the supported/refused alternatives. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features - [Pipeline operator](../operators-and-syntax/pipeline-operator.md) — whole-value function application, distinct from per-item mapping. - [method-call-operator.md](../operators-and-syntax/method-call-operator.md) — the third `=?>` member of the family, deferred for semantic (not naming) churn. - [fn-scan.md](../experimental/fn-scan.md) — the "consolidated before stabilization" sibling class (`scan-left`/`scan-right` → `fn:scan`); the same rule applies: old shapes do not parse. *Entry created 2026-10-10 (REQ-126 scaffold).*
